amenitiesDescription:
Rooftop: A forty-foot heated lap pool with covered cabanas and an observation deck reading across the canopy to Biscayne Bay and the Downtown skyline. Summer kitchens with outdoor grills and long tables sit alongside a lounge seating area for private events, and an outdoor yoga and meditation terrace occupies the quiet end.

Wellness: A zen spa-inspired level with sauna, steam room and hot and cold plunge tubs, a powder room with shower and dressing area, and a state-of-the-art fitness centre opening onto planting.

Residents' lounge: A co-working lounge and media area on the mezzanine, with a golf simulator and a multi-purpose pool table.

Pets and services: An enclosed private dog park and a private grooming room. Building services include a 24/7 front desk with night security, monitoring and surveillance, valet parking, on-site management and maintenance, a dedicated secured parcel room, an enclosed bicycle room, EV-ready parking, an emergency generator, and private storage rooms available for purchase.

investmentThesis:
Coconut Grove is the tightest luxury supply in Miami-Dade, and not by accident: zoning and tree canopy protections cap what can be approved, so the pipeline is measured in single buildings. The Lincoln, OPUS and Ziggurat together add fewer than ninety homes to the village core. That constraint is the whole investment case here — it is written into the code, not into a brochure.

The $58 million construction loan from SME Capital, arranged by Berkadia and closed in September 2026, retires the financing question on a Q3 2028 delivery. The developers had already put the site on their own balance sheet, acquiring it for $8.56 million in 2023, and were 40 percent pre-sold before the loan funded. LORE Development Group was formed by the Brazilian asset managers Leste Group and Opportunity, and partners here with Miami-based Element Development.

What separates this building from its Grove neighbours is the entry point. Ziggurat opens at $3.5 million across nineteen homes, OPUS at $2.8 million across fourteen, and Vita at Grove Isle at $8.5 million; The Lincoln opens at $1.5 million, with a released band running to $3.1 million. For a buyer who wants a walkable Grove address without moving up into estate pricing, this is one of very few ways in — and at forty-eight homes, the owner roster stays short.

name: The Lincoln Coconut Grove
parking: Valet parking; EV-ready garage; enclosed bicycle room; private storage available for purchase
residenceContent:
Eight stories on a 20,970-square-foot corner where Lincoln Avenue meets SW 27th Avenue, a three-minute walk from the restaurants, shops and marinas at the centre of Coconut Grove. Frank Paredes drew the building as a set of stacked, rounded bays rather than a flat slab, and Cité Arquitetura of Rio de Janeiro consulted on the façade: vertical timber-toned fins wrap the corners, and every balcony carries a planted edge, so the elevation reads as canopy rather than curtain wall. Arrival is under a covered entrance off Lincoln Avenue, into a double-height lobby with a sculptural stair up to the mezzanine.

Forty-eight homes run from one bedroom to four, and every plan in the building carries an in-suite den or office in addition to its bedrooms — the reason the bathroom counts sit high for the bedroom count. Ceilings reach eleven feet. Porcelain floors run throughout with three alternative finishes available, eight-foot doors are hung on concealed hinges, and balconies are glass-railed with power outlets and space to plant. Kitchens are Snaidero, made in Italy, with islands up to ten feet, quartz counters, integrated panelled Miele appliances and a built-in wine fridge; Sub-Zero and Wolf are optional upgrades. Primary bathrooms carry marble counters, floor-to-ceiling glass shower panels, Brizo fixtures and Toto fittings.

The top floor holds six duplex penthouses, from 2,713 to 2,983 square feet of interior space, oriented north-west, west, south-west, north-east, east and south-east. Above them the roof is given over entirely to residents: a forty-foot heated lap pool, an observation deck with covered cabanas, summer kitchens with grills and long tables, an outdoor yoga and meditation area, and lounge seating under pergolas. The building is designed to a green building certification, with an emergency generator, EV-ready parking and 24/7 front desk and night security.
